([[Hazel Green, Alabama]]) | college = [[Alabama Crimson Tide men's basketball|Alabama]] (2018–2020) | draft_year = 2020 | draft_round = 1 | draft_pick = 13 | draft_team = [[New Orleans Pelicans]] | career_start = 2020 | years1 = {{nbay|2020|start}}–{{nbay|2023|end}} | team1 = [[New Orleans Pelicans]] | years2 = [[2022–23 NBA G League season|2022]]–[[2023–24 NBA G League season|2024]] | team2 = →[[Birmingham Squadron]] | years3 = {{nbay|2023|end}} | team3 = [[Toronto Raptors]] | years4 = [[2023–24 NBA G League season|2024]] | team4 = →[[Raptors 905]] | years5 = {{nbay|2023|end}} | team5 = [[Utah Jazz]] | years6 = [[2024–25 NBA G League season|2024–2025]] | team6 = [[Capital City Go-Go]] | years7 = [[2025–26 NBA G League season|2025]]–present | team7 = [[Wisconsin Herd]] | highlights = * First-team All-[[Southeastern Conference|SEC]] (2020) * SEC All-Freshman Team (2019) | medal_templates = {{MedalSport|Men's basketball}} {{MedalCountry|{{bk|USA}}}} {{MedalCompetition|[[FIBA Under-19 Basketball World Cup|FIBA Under-19 World Cup]]}} {{MedalGold|[[2019 FIBA Under-19 Basketball World Cup|2019 Greece]]|[[United States men's national under-19 basketball team|Team]]}} }} '''Kira Aundrea Lewis Jr.''' ({{IPAc-en|ˈ|k|aɪ|r|ə}} {{respell|KY|rə}};{{cite press release|title=2023-24 start of season NBA pronunciation guide|url=https://www.nba.com/news/2023-24-start-of-season-nba-pronunciation-guide|website=NBA.com|date=October 24, 2023|access-date=May 18, 2024}} born April 6, 2001) is an American professional [[basketball]] player for the [[Wisconsin Herd]] of the [[NBA G League]]. He played [[college basketball]] for the [[Alabama Crimson Tide men's basketball|Alabama Crimson Tide]] and was drafted by the [[New Orleans Pelicans]] in the first round of the [[2020 NBA draft]]. ==High school career== Lewis played basketball for [[Hazel Green High School]] in [[Hazel Green, Alabama]] for three years. As a junior, he averaged 28.5 points, 5.9 rebounds, 4.5 assists, and 3.9 steals per game and led his team to the Alabama Class 6A semifinals. Lewis earned first-team All-State honors for his second consecutive season, was a finalist for [[Alabama Mr. Basketball]], and was named [[Huntsville, Alabama|Huntsville]] Region Player of the Year and Alabama Class 6A Player of the Year.{{cite web |last=Boyette |first=Daniel |title=Hazel Green's Kira Lewis stepped up as leader, earns Huntsville top basketball honor |url=https://www.al.com/highschoolsports/article/hazel-greens-kira-lewis-is-the-huntsville-region-boys-basketball-player-of-the-year/ |website=AL.com |access-date=December 3, 2019 |date=March 20, 2018}} He was originally in the 2019 class but graduated early from high school and [[reclassification (education)|reclassified]] to 2018.{{cite web |title=Alabama Men's Basketball Signs Kira Lewis, will Enroll in Classes this Fall |url=https://rolltide.com/news/2018/8/15/alabama-mens-basketball-signs-kira-lewis-will-enroll-in-classes-this-fall.aspx |publisher=University of Alabama Athletics |access-date=December 3, 2019 |date=August 15, 2018}} On August 10, 2018, Lewis committed to [[Alabama Crimson Tide men's basketball|Alabama]] over several major [[NCAA Division I]] offers, including from [[Indiana Hoosiers men's basketball|Indiana]] and [[Kansas Jayhawks men's basketball|Kansas]]. He was considered a four-star [[college recruiting|recruit]] by [[ESPN]] and [[247Sports]].{{cite web |last=Daniels |first=Evan |title=Kira Lewis commits to Alabama, reclassifies to 2018 |url=https://247sports.com/college/basketball/recruiting/Article/Kira-Lewis-commits-to-Alabama-reclassifies-to-2018-120549701/ |publisher=[[247Sports.com|247Sports]] |access-date=December 3, 2019 |date=August 10, 2018}} ==College career== In his freshman season with Alabama, Lewis, at age 17, was the second-youngest player in NCAA Division I basketball behind Everett Perrot of [[Pepperdine Waves men's basketball|Pepperdine]] and was the youngest player to appear in a game. Lewis scored six points in his first career game versus [[2018–19 Southern Jaguars basketball team|Southern]]. The following game, he had 21 points against [[2018–19 Appalachian State Mountaineers men's basketball team|Appalachian State]] and followed that up with a season-high 24 points against [[2018–19 Wichita State Shockers men's basketball team|Wichita State]].{{cite magazine |last=Walsh |first=Christopher |title=The talk about Kira Lewis Jr. is shifting from his age to his consistency |url=https://www.si.com/college/alabama/bamacentral/the-talk-about-kira-lewis-jr-is-shifting-from-his-age-to-his-consistency-VlPcBLHfAkeYII-cLqCZAQ/ |magazine=[[Sports Illustrated]] |access-date=December 3, 2019 |date=January 22, 2019}} He tied his season high of 24 points against [[2018–19 Georgia Bulldogs basketball team|Georgia]] in February 2019.{{cite news |last=Casagrande |first=Michael |title=Kira Lewis is staying at Alabama after flirting with transfer |url=https://www.al.com/alabamabasketball/2019/04/kira-lewis-is-staying-at-alabama-after-flirting-with-transfer.html |access-date=December 10, 2019 |work=Al.com |date=April 8, 2019}} Lewis averaged 13.5 points, 2.9 assists, and 2.6 rebounds per game and was named to the [[Southeastern Conference|SEC]] All-Freshman Team. However, Alabama struggled and finished 18–16, losing in the first round of the NIT. Lewis entered the transfer portal before new coach [[Nate Oats]] convinced him to return.{{cite magazine |last=Martin |first=Tyler |title=Alabama Will Look to an Older, More Experienced Kira Lewis Jr. for Success Under Nate Oats |url=https://www.si.com/college/alabama/bamacentral/alabama-basketball-kira-lewis-jr-nate-oats/ |access-date=December 10, 2019 |magazine=[[Sports Illustrated]] |date=October 25, 2019}} In his sophomore season opener, Lewis scored a then-career-high 30 points in an 81–80 loss to [[2019–20 Penn Quakers men's basketball team|Penn]].{{cite news |title=Dingle lifts Penn to 81–80 opening win over Alabama |url=https://www.espn.com/mens-college-basketball/recap?gameId=401169798 |access-date=December 10, 2019 |work=[[ESPN]] |agency=[[Associated Press]] |date=November 5, 2019}} He scored a career-high 37 points on February 8, 2020, in a 105–102 overtime win against [[2019–20 Georgia Bulldogs basketball team|Georgia]].{{cite news |title=Lewis scores career-high 37 as Alabama tops Georgia in OT |url=https://www.espn.com/mens-college-basketball/recap?gameId=401166337 |access-date=August 24, 2020 |work=[[ESPN]] |agency=[[Associated Press]] |date=February 8, 2020}} On February 12, Lewis became the first Alabama player since 1996 to record a [[triple-double]], posting 10 points, 10 rebounds and 13 assists in a 95–91 overtime loss to [[2019–20 Auburn Tigers men's basketball team|Auburn]]. He became the second player in school history to reach this accomplishment.{{cite news |title=Wiley, No. 11 Auburn survive in OT again, 95–91 over Alabama |url=https://www.espn.com/mens-college-basketball/recap?gameId=401166344 |access-date=August 24, 2020 |work=[[ESPN]] |agency=[[Associated Press]] |date=February 12, 2020}} On February 25, Lewis contributed 29 points, seven rebounds, and four assists in an 80–73 loss to [[2019–20 Mississippi State Bulldogs men's basketball team|Mississippi State]].{{cite news |last=Stephens |first=Hannah |title=Alabama loses game, John Petty against Miss State |url=https://rolltidewire.usatoday.com/2020/02/25/alabama-loses-game-john-petty-against-miss-state/ |access-date=February 27, 2020 |work=Roll Tide Wire |date=February 25, 2020}} At the conclusion of the regular season, Lewis was named to the First Team All-SEC.{{cite press release|url=https://www.secsports.com/article/28877731/sec-announces-2020-men-basketball-awards |title=SEC announces 2020 Men's Basketball Awards |publisher=Southeastern Conference |date=March 10, 2020 |access-date=March 10, 2020}} As a sophomore, Lewis averaged 18.5 points, 4.8 rebounds, and 5.2 assists per game.{{cite web |last=Tsoukalas |first=Tony |title=How to watch: Alabama basketball vs Tennessee in the SEC Tournament |url=https://alabama.rivals.com/news/how-to-watch-alabama-basketball-vs-tennessee-in-the-sec-tournament |website=Rivals.com |date=March 11, 2020 |access-date=March 22, 2020}} After the season, Lewis declared for the [[2020 NBA draft]].{{cite web |last=Potter |first=Charlie |title=Alabama's Kira Lewis, John Petty to test NBA draft waters |url=https://247sports.com/college/alabama/Article/Alabama-Basketball-Kira-Lewis-John-Petty-to-test-NBA-draft-waters-145346895/ |website=247 Sports |date=March 24, 2020|access-date=March 25, 2020}} ==Professional career== ===New Orleans Pelicans (2020–2024)=== Lewis was selected with the 13th pick in the [[2020 NBA draft]] by the [[New Orleans Pelicans]].{{cite news|first=Kevin|last=Flaherty|title=Pelicans pick Alabama's Kira Lewis at No. 13 in NBA draft|url=https://247sports.com/Article/2020-NBA-Draft-New-Orleans-Pelicans-Kira-Lewis-Alabama-basketball-154960904/|work=247 Sports|date=November 18, 2020|access-date=November 18, 2020}} On November 30, 2020, he signed with the Pelicans.{{cite web|title=New Orleans Pelicans sign Kira Lewis Jr.|url=https://www.nba.com/pelicans/news/new-orleans-pelicans-sign-kira-lewis-jr-contract|website=NBA.com|date=November 30, 2020|access-date=December 2, 2020}} Lewis was a rotational player to start the year. His first career game with double-digit scoring came January 13, 2021 against the [[2020–21 Los Angeles Clippers season|Los Angeles Clippers]]. He had 10 points that game. He registered a career-high 16 points and 6 assists on March 23 against the [[2020–21 Los Angeles Lakers season|Los Angeles Lakers]]. On December 8, 2021, Lewis tore his ACL and sprained his MCL during a 114–120 overtime loss to the [[2021–22 Denver Nuggets season|Denver Nuggets]], ending his season.{{cite news|first=Andrew|last=Lopez|title=New Orleans Pelicans' Kira Lewis out for season after tearing ACL|url=https://www.espn.com/nba/story/_/id/32830802|work=[[ESPN]]|date=December 9, 2021|access-date=December 9, 2021}} ===Toronto Raptors (2024)=== On January 17, 2024, Lewis and a 2024 second-round pick were traded by the Pelicans to the [[Indiana Pacers]] in exchange for cash considerations,{{cite web|title=New Orleans Pelicans complete trade with Indiana Pacers|url=https://www.nba.com/pelicans/news/new-orleans-pelicans-complete-trade-with-indiana-pacers|website=NBA.com|date=January 17, 2024|access-date=January 17, 2024}} before being traded to the [[Toronto Raptors]], along with [[Bruce Brown (basketball)|Bruce Brown]], [[Jordan Nwora]] and three first-round picks in exchange for [[Pascal Siakam]].{{cite web|title=RAPTORS COMPLETE TRADE WITH INDIANA|url=https://www.nba.com/raptors/news/raptors-complete-trade-with-indiana-2|website=NBA.com|date=January 17, 2024|access-date=January 18, 2024}} On January 19, 2024, the Raptors assigned Lewis to the [[Raptors 905]] of the [[NBA G League]].{{cite web|title=Raptors assign Lewis Jr. to Raptors 905|url= https://www.tsn.ca/toronto-raptors-assign-kira-lewis-jr-to-g-league-s-raptors-905-1.2065031?tsn-amp |website=NBA.com|date=January 19, 2024|access-date=January 20, 2024}} ===Utah Jazz (2024)=== After playing only two minutes in one game with the Raptors, Lewis was traded to the [[Utah Jazz]] alongside [[Otto Porter Jr.]] and a 2024 first-round pick in exchange for [[Kelly Olynyk]] and [[Ochai Agbaji]].{{cite web|title=Utah Jazz Acquire Kira Lewis Jr., Otto Porter Jr., and a Future Draft Pick from Toronto Raptors|url=https://www.nba.com/jazz/news/utah-jazz-acquire-kira-lewis-jr-otto-porter-jr-and-a-future-draft-pick-from-toronto-raptors|website=NBA.com|date=February 8, 2024|access-date=February 8, 2024}} ===Capital City Go-Go (2024–2025)=== Lewis joined the [[Houston Rockets]] for the [[2024 NBA Summer League]]. On September 29, 2024, Lewis signed with the [[Washington Wizards]],{{cite web|title=Wizards Announce 2024 Training Camp Roster/Schedule|url=https://www.nba.com/wizards/news/wizards-announce-2024-training-camp-roster-schedule|website=NBA.com|date=September 29, 2024|access-date=September 30, 2024}} but was waived on October 12.{{cite tweet|author=Wizards PR|title=Official: The Washington Wizards have waived G Kira Lewis Jr. and F Leaky Black.|number=1845129032238608612|user=WizPRStats|date=October 12, 2024|access-date=October 13, 2024}} On October 28, he joined the [[Capital City Go-Go]].{{cite web|title=Go-Go Announce Training Camp Roster, Dates|url=https://capitalcity.gleague.nba.com/news/go-go-announce-training-camp-roster-dates-2|website=NBA.com|date=October 28, 2024|access-date=November 3, 2024}} Lewis joined the [[Miami Heat]] for the [[2025 NBA Summer League]]. ===Wisconsin Herd (2025–present)=== On November 7, 2025, Lewis was named to the [[Wisconsin Herd]] opening night roster.{{cite web|url=https://wisconsin.gleague.nba.com/news/wisconsin-herd-announces-2025-26-opening-night-roster|title=WISCONSIN HERD ANNOUNCES 2025-26 OPENING NIGHT ROSTER|website=gleague.nba.com|date=November 7, 2025|access-date=November 7, 2025}} ==National team career== Lewis played for the [[United States men's national under-19 basketball team|United States]] at the [[2019 FIBA Under-19 Basketball World Cup|2019 FIBA Under-19 World Cup]] in [[Heraklion]], Greece. He averaged four points and 1.6 assists per game and helped his team win a gold medal.{{cite web|first=Paloma|last=Villicana|title=Kira Lewis brings back gold to north Alabama|url=https://www.waff.com/2019/07/09/kira-lewis-brings-back-gold-north-alabama/|website=WAFF.com|publisher=[[WAFF (TV)|WAFF]]|date=July 8, 2019|access-date=December 3, 2019}} ==Career
